title: Legendre's Conjecture: Prime Between n² and (n+1)²

problemStatement.plain: Legendre's conjecture (1798) asserts there is always a prime between consecutive perfect squares. One of Landau's four problems; open. Verified computationally to n ≤ 1.5 × 10^18.
whyMatters: Landau problem (1912) — one of four 'unattackable' problems
Equivalent to prime gap bound g(p_k) ≤ 2√p_k + 1
Not implied by RH (RH gives only g ≪ √p log p, one log too weak)
Connection to Cramér heuristic on prime gaps

proven: Verified computationally for n ≤ 1.5 × 10^18 (Nicely et al.)
In this repo, legendre-partial verified n = 1, …, 20 via native_decide
Baker–Harman–Pintz (2001): primes in [x, x + x^0.525] — does not reach Legendre
knownResults.goal: Initial survey; identify tractable sub-milestone for iteration 2 (recommended: equivalence with prime-gap bound)

currentState.focus: S4-ACT-α DONE (researcher-1, 2026-06-06): formalized the salvageable one-way implication identified by iter-4 PREP-1 audit. New file proofs/Proofs/LegendrePrimeGapSqrtBoundSuffices.lean (227 LOC, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, Docker build verified) proves: (∀ k, Nat.nth Nat.Prime (k+1) - Nat.nth Nat.Prime k ≤ 2 * Nat.sqrt (Nat.nth Nat.Prime k) + 1) → LegendreConjecture. Uses Nat.findGreatest on the predicate 'nth Prime k ≤ n²' to extract the largest prime ≤ n², compositeness of n² for n ≥ 2 to get strict inequality nth Prime k < n², and the iter-2 form equivalences for three free corollaries (gap/distance/half-open).
currentState.nextAction: S5 ACT — Cramér ⇒ Legendre (Sub-Milestone A). Now that prime_gap_sqrt_bound_implies_legendre is in place, the route Cramér ⇒ Legendre factors cleanly: state Cramér's conjecture as a hypothesis, derive that C·(log p_k)² ≤ 2·√p_k + 1 for sufficiently large k (asymptotics), bridge the finite-tail base cases via legendre-partial, then compose with this iteration's theorem. Estimated size: +200-250 LOC. 0 new axioms expected (only Cramér as hypothesis). Target file: proofs/Proofs/CramerImpliesLegendre.lean.

builtItems.summary: Four equivalent forms of Legendre's Conjecture (original / gap / distance / half-open); three global iffs; sample transferrals of the partial cases.

One-way implication PrimeGapSqrtBound → LegendreConjecture (+ three corollaries for gap/distance/half-open forms). Salvageable half of the iter-3 proposed iff after the iter-4 PREP-1 audit found the other direction unprovable from LegendreConjecture alone.

insights: Legendre is NOT implied by RH — Cramér's RH-based bound g ≪ √p log p has an extra logarithmic factor relative to what Legendre needs
Bertrand's postulate is too weak by a factor of ~n: it gives a prime in (n², 2n²) but Legendre needs the prime in (n², (n+1)²) — an interval of length 2n+1, vs Bertrand's interval of length n²
Best unconditional short-interval result (Baker–Harman–Pintz 2001) is θ = 0.525, still missing Legendre's θ = 0.5

The proposed iff Legendre ↔ ∀ k, p_{k+1}-p_k ≤ 2·√p_k + 1 is NOT a true equivalence: forward direction (Legendre ⇒ gap bound) yields only ≤ 4·√p_k + 2 in the worst case (iter-4 PREP-1 audit). The salvageable reverse direction is the actual mathematical content.

The reverse direction (PrimeGapSqrtBound ⇒ LegendreConjecture) is now formalized in Lean (iter-5, axiom-free) using Nat.findGreatest to extract the largest prime ≤ n² plus the compositeness of n² for n ≥ 2.
Mathlib lacks a primeGap definition; introducing one would benefit other gallery proofs
mathlibGaps: No short-interval prime theorems (Hoheisel, Huxley, BHP)
No Legendre conjecture statement (only the partial version in legendre-partial)
nextSteps: Sub-Milestone A (now newly tractable): formalize Cramér ⇒ Legendre eventually via the iter-5 prime_gap_sqrt_bound_implies_legendre theorem (Cramér ⇒ sqrt-bound for large k, plus legendre-partial for small k)
Sub-Milestone C: extend native_decide verification to n ≤ 100 (low value)

approaches.name: Form equivalences (Sub-Milestone B basic)
approaches.hypothesis: Legendre is equivalent at the form level to gap/distance/half-open reformulations, providable structurally via (n+1)² = n² + 2n + 1
approaches.strategy: Pointwise iffs LegendreAt n ↔ LegendreGapAt n etc., then lift to global iffs
risks: Pure structural rewriting may be judged too trivial for a separate deliverable

approaches.hypothesis: PrimeGapSqrtBound (∀ k, p_{k+1} - p_k ≤ 2·√p_k + 1) implies LegendreConjecture — the salvageable direction of the originally proposed iff
